newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE-CAMINERO AIMS TO BREAK DERBY JINX.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-CAMINERO AIMS TO BREAK DERBY JINX.

text.p: Atletico Madrid midfielder Jose
Luis Caminero is almost certain to start Saturday's big game
against Real Madrid in the Spanish league and hopes to break a
jinx on his encounters with his former club.
Last year's double-winners struggled at the beginning of the
season in the absence of their influential playmaker, but have
gone 10 games without defeat since his return from injury and
could close the gap on leaders Real to five points.
After being written off just two months ago, the turnaround
is already a major triumph for coach Radomir Antic's men.
But on a crucial weekend of league action, a Real win
together with defeat for second-placed Barcelona at
fourth-placed Real Betis could leave coach Fabio Capello's side
a daunting six points clear at the top.
Caminero has never won in the three games he has started
against Real, and was sent off in last year's match in the
Santiago Bernabeu stadium, having missed three derbies through
injury or suspension.
The news of Caminero's recovery from an injury picked up in
scoring last Sunday came as Atletico saw their plans to prepare
the match in the club's favourite sierra retreat dashed by heavy
wind and rain.
As a result Radomir Antic's squad spent much of Thursday in
a bus after driving to the hotel, and then returning to train in
the Spanish capital.
Antic will wait to announce his squad until soccer
authorities have ruled on an appeal against a three-match
suspension imposed on Argentine midfielder Diego Simeone for
stamping on Julen Guerrero of Athletic Bilbao.
But Atletico have been boosted by the news that key Real
defender Fernando Hierro was a doubtful starter after picking up
a knock in midweek Cup action.
Hierro figures in the team list that Antic's opposite
number, Capello, put out on Friday. But the Spanish
international is expected to take a late fitness test.
Hierro's absence would create a major gap at the back for
Real, where Capello has already shaken things up by bringing in
newly-signed defender Christian Panucci.
As one of the teams to have conceded most headed goals in
the Spanish league, the absence of a big man at the back could
leave Real vulnerable to strikes in the air from Atletico
forward Kiko Narvaez.
Derby games are rarely ill-tempered affairs, but despite
being refereed by the Spanish division's youngest match
official, Real and Atletico could be excused for thinking they
are in the hands of a man born to the job.
Eduardo Iturralde, 29, is the grandson of a referee who took
charge of no less than six Madrid derbies in the 1940s.
Atletico, then Spain's leading side, won four of the games, and
Real the other two.
The 1997 fixture is already a sell-out, with Ajax manager
Louis van Gaal -- a man widely tipped to replace Bobby Robson at
Barcelona -- expected to make the trip from his side's Spanish
training camp.
But one fan who will not be turning up is the leader of
Real's hard-core supporters group the Ultrasur, who has been
given a 500,000 peseta ($3,820) fine and a two-year ban for
bringing a catapult and three metal bolts to a Real game. It was
the last of a series of offences.
